games.premise: An epic fantasy RPG that is entirely character creation. Rite after rite, tutorial after tutorial, guided by a delighted floating orb named Glim — who has been here longer than you and is starting to notice
games.state: Job 1 only: the creation flow through to a loading bar that never finishes. The tutorial engine, the procedural stretch and Glim's unravelling are all unbuilt. Trevor's concept, Fable 5's build. Authored defects are registered in its `CLAUDE.md` — read it before fixing anything
games.title: ÆTHERMOOR — Chronicles of the Ninefold Throne

games.premise: Missile Command at dusk over a city that is going dark — your interceptor blooms and then *lingers*, and the lingering cloud doesn't kill, it takes a missile's guidance away and lets physics finish it
games.state: About half built. Engine, city, damage, build phase, two weapons and three threats are done. **Loss tinted by beauty is the whole point** — no repair, no victory, no people, ever; the rejected repair mechanic and the no-people rule are both registered in its `CLAUDE.md`, read it first. Thermite, the intended visual signature, exists as a dev-gated visual prototype only; weapons, threats and the light-pollution system are planned
games.title: AFTERGLOW

games.premise: Qix as celestial cartography — fence off the void, capture the constellation's stars, watch the figure ink itself in gold
games.state: Complete and playable at nine maps. Designed end-to-end by Fable 5 with no human design input; the 3-map original is preserved and **locked** — read its `CLAUDE.md` before touching anything
games.title: ASTERISM — a charting of the heavens

games.premise: SMB world 1 as a steamed bun on a giant kitchen counter. Built for a friend of Trevor's
games.state: Two levels, playable end-to-end with progression between them. 1-2 is the underground — the cupboard under the counter, with cracker lifts and a door you walk out into the light. A console test harness in `tools/` autopilots both levels; re-run it before trusting any change to `TUNE` or a layout, and read its `CLAUDE.md` first
games.title: Bao's Big Breakfast

games.premise: **blocks, i guess** — a thirteen-second joke about a developer who couldn't be bothered. Someone upends a bag of tetrominoes into a box, they pile up, you top out, and a random number is your score. You never get to do anything
games.state: Complete, and meant to be. **Nearly everything visible is an authored defect** — there is no CSS at all, the options menu is dead, the leaderboard is unsorted and never resets — so read its `CLAUDE.md` before "fixing" a single thing. Two parts are sincere: a real impulse-based rigid-body solver, which is the whole joke's counterweight and must not be simplified, and the rule that the player never gets a verb. `validate.js` has 43 assertions and **asserts the jokes as spec** — it goes red if someone adds a stylesheet or sorts the leaderboard — which is worth stealing for any parody build. It also registers one real, invisible physics defect found while writing it. Open to copy and fine-tuning, closed to features
games.title: blocks, i guess

games.premise: Build a battle bot, press GO, watch it fight on its own
games.state: Sandbox pass: physics, component damage, behavior chips, three win conditions. No economy yet

games.premise: Asteroids where the gun is also a thruster — no brakes, every shot shoves you back, and the screen-clearing pulse gets likelier to kill you every time you use it
games.state: Mostly finished across four modes. Predates most of the conventions here and set some of them. Scores now persist; audio is the main gap and RIDICULOUS still wants playtesting. Recoil is original and untouchable — read its `CLAUDE.md`
games.title: DRIFT

games.premise: Newtonian dueling with no brakes, played dead straight as a Western gunslinger picture — outlaws, wanted posters, high noon, and a game that never once admits you're flying a spaceship
games.state: Third shape: was a duel, became a flight sandbox, now pivoting back to a duel (2026-08-05). The **sandbox file is the current build and it works**; all of v3 is unbuilt. Pure Newtonian, zero damping — that's the identity, don't add drag. A CPU that can fly it is the unsolved gate. Concept lives in the `dead-reckoning-concept` skill; read its `CLAUDE.md` first

games.premise: Dead Space: Block Party! — a fake licensed Tetris tie-in whose cheerfulness is the horror
games.state: Ported to standalone HTML and playable end-to-end. Authored defects are registered in its `CLAUDE.md` — read it before fixing anything. Wants audio and more tips
games.title: Dead Space: Block Party!

games.premise: A faithful-ish remake of Gem Tower Defense, the lost flash classic — maze the path with blocks, keep one of every five as a gem, and combine gems into 13 advanced towers
games.state: Mechanically complete and playable endlessly. Reconstructed from two stats workbooks that live in the folder, so **read its `CLAUDE.md` for source precedence before changing any number** — and note the 40/40 recipe bijection that any recipe edit breaks silently. Air waves every 4th level are the difficulty and are meant to be. Wants a background pass, score persistence, and difficulty modes
games.title: GEM TD

games.premise: A modern artillery duel where seeing is the whole game — you're a dug-in gun that can't move, hunting another one you can't see, through per-column fog you have to buy with a recon drone and shell out of the treeline
games.state: Playable and winnable, but not yet a contest. Fog, concealment and drone optics are the finished part. **The enemy is an explicit placeholder that fires on a timer and doesn't know you exist** — the real muzzle-flash counterbattery was built once and pulled for being too lethal to playtest, and rebuilding it (with a dev mode) is the next job. Immobility is the thesis, not a gap; long-term target is player/CPU symmetry. Read its `CLAUDE.md`
games.title: GREY ZONE — Job 3: Engagement

games.premise: Galaga with weapon powerups — seven guns that each fire completely differently
games.state: Playable; wants a balance overhaul (player far too strong)

games.premise: A Civil War battle where you are the general standing on the field, and every order has to be carried to the regiment by hand — distance is latency. Under it, a line of battle that bends, stretches, tears open and closes up
games.state: **A kernel, not a game.** Four jobs, two systems: the line mechanic, and the courier — a drag writes an order, a rider carries it, and nothing reaches the troops until he arrives. Enemy, volleys, morale and ammunition are unbuilt, and nearly everything visible is placeholder — read the register in its `CLAUDE.md` before "fixing" the palette or the scale, and `DESIGN.md` before picking a job. Sibling to the unported **Volley**, which it may eventually combine with

games.state: Pass 1: the object is built — case, wear, and a working 62-segment reflective display. Game loop is a sandbox only. Authored defects (stuck segment, case damage) are registered in its `CLAUDE.md` — read it before fixing anything

games.state: Playable end-to-end at six towers, six threats, one map, 50 waves. Sincere and affectionate, and the Anthropic palette is the joke. **The economy runs away and most runs win easily** — diagnosis in its `CLAUDE.md`. Wide open for depth: more towers, threats and maps

games.state: Two prototypes, neither carried forward — v1 (Opus 4.8) is the deeper sim, v2 (Fable 5) feels closer. **Trench building is the unsolved gate** and nothing downstream matters until it lands; the diagnosis and a v3 proposal are in its `CLAUDE.md`. games.premise: The whole WotC-era Pokémon TCG — every card, played to the letter of the original ruleset. Win matches, win packs, build decks from what you actually own, fill a dex
games.state: The biggest project here by far, and the only one with a build step: **`shadowless.html` is generated from `src/`, so never hand-edit it.** Jobs 1–9 are done and three sets are live at 221 of 221 cards — a ladder of named challengers, packs of whichever set you are on, cosmetic variants, a dex and a deck builder, all persisted. Six suites plus a screenshotter, because the smoke stub has no layout engine. **Read its `CLAUDE.md` first** — the depth is in twenty-two siblings and a `Rulings/` folder, and that tree is the thing most worth stealing from this repo: `MAINTENANCE.md` is how a doc tree gets un-drifted, `PLAYTEST.md` is how to work a bug report from a human, and `HISTORY.md` keeps rejected ideas with the reason each one lost
games.title: Shadowless — a WotC-era Pokémon TCG

games.premise: Snake, drawn badly on purpose in ballpoint pen on notebook paper, with googly eyes
games.state: Reskin pass complete and playable. **Shedding is built but explicitly undecided** — drop segments to escape a box you drew yourself into. Its `CLAUDE.md` carries two falsifiable predictions and a **trap trainer** (`T`) that arms fixed, hand-verified death positions so feel can be A/B'd against the same board instead of across two different runs. Worth stealing for any game where a mechanic has to be judged by feel

games.state: Mostly finished. Physics are pure classic Pong and must stay that way; authored annoyances and an honesty rule for anything the CPU does are registered in its `CLAUDE.md`. More ad copy welcome
